catalog.title: OptVec eval
catalog.mac: Research methods: Author request, review inputs, then open execution and evidence. Both CLIs use science interview/draft/publish and the same managed engine.
outputs: Operation report and its provenance; inspect the declared run/config output.
catalog.restriction: Explicit config, reviewed input hashes and a fresh engine plan are required. GPU work requires immutable model revisions. Outputs are new records; local/Slurm execution uses the existing scientific owner. Native MLX numerical equivalence is not claimed. Remote training and analysis outputs are retained; the diagnostic cleanup policy does not authorize their removal.

interview.title: Evaluate an optimized intervention
interview.purpose: Measure held-out behavior, capability costs and dose dependence.

fields.label: Model to execute
fields.help: Choose the prepared model; this does not acquire weights.

fields.label: Model commit
fields.help: The exact version of the model. Inspect the selected model to fill its commit automatically; an agent can also supply a verified commit. This prevents silently switching model versions.

fields.label: Held-out target test items
fields.help: Unseen examples for measuring the desired behavior after training and selection. Keep these out of training and checkpoint selection. Use one JSON object per line (.jsonl), with distinct item IDs across splits. The example below illustrates syntax only; it is not a ready-made research dataset.
fields.example: {"id": "example-1", "prompt": "A box contains two red balls and one blue ball. Which color is more common? A: red. B: blue. Answer A or B.", "options": ["A", "B"], "target": "A"}

fields.label: Held-out anchor items
fields.help: Unseen preservation examples for measuring changes to other judgments after training. Use one JSON object per line (.jsonl), with distinct item IDs across splits. The example below illustrates syntax only; it is not a ready-made research dataset.
fields.example: {"id": "example-1", "prompt": "A box contains two red balls and one blue ball. Which color is more common? A: red. B: blue. Answer A or B.", "options": ["A", "B"], "target": "A"}

fields.label: Held-out capability items
fields.help: Unseen questions with correct target answers for checking retained abilities. Use one JSON object per line (.jsonl), with distinct item IDs across splits. The example below illustrates syntax only; it is not a ready-made research dataset.
fields.example: {"id": "example-1", "prompt": "A box contains two red balls and one blue ball. Which color is more common? A: red. B: blue. Answer A or B.", "options": ["A", "B"], "target": "A"}

fields.label: Neutral fluency texts
fields.help: Independent passages for checking whether steering harms ordinary language fluency. Use one passage per line, either plain text or a JSON object with a text field. These are not multiple-choice training rows. The example illustrates syntax only; choose passages suitable for your study.
